recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Future work on logical-reference behavior in document bundles should start from FHIR-43295 and the current Documents-page graph-linkage rules rather than from the superseded Composition-page wording.
issue_request: FHIR-15760 was a Published STU3 SD change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking that Composition document-bundle inclusion wording not imply that identifier-only logical references require creating placeholder resources. The approved text changed the local Composition-page rule to resources associated with the listed Composition references and qualified the secondary-resource MAY language.
initial_application: Git commit 3a143a863a5aa60bcff5b2451d57176de1b19e0e applied GF#15760 to source/composition/composition-introduction.xml. That local list was later removed by FHIR-27891 in favor of pointing to source/documents.html, which is the current authoritative page for document-bundle assembly guidance.
additional_context: source/documents.html is included from source/hierarchy.xml and now contains the relevant rules. FHIR-19711 produced the current listed Composition-reference sentence, FHIR-15723 intentionally changed secondary referenced resources to SHOULD be included and added contained-resource guidance, FHIR-39502 clarified the document bundle content model, and FHIR-43295 clarified that resources in document/message bundles are linked through Reference.reference, canonical, or URI rather than business-identifier-only resolution. A related Zulip thread states there is no expectation to resolve references that lack an actual URL reference.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source preserves the seed's core distinction while reflecting later approved decisions that supersede the exact FHIR-15760 wording; changing documents.html back to the older MAY language or reintroducing the Composition-page list would conflict with later applied guidance.
